cluster.rationale: Reference value used for association; not a security configuration.

configs.description: Configuration for the topic that are overridden from the cluster defaults. The key of the map is a Kafka topic property name, for example: 'cleanup.policy=compact', 'compression.type=producer'.
configs.rationale: Certain configs (e.g., `retention.ms`, `cleanup.policy`, `compression.type`) may leak data or allow unbounded data growth if misconfigured.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can destroy the resource on 'destroy'/'apply'. Setting to 'PREVENT' guards against accidental topic deletion; policy should whitelist 'PREVENT' for production topics.

location.description: ID of the location of the Kafka resource. See https://cloud.google.com/managed-kafka/docs/locations for a list of supported locations.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

partition_count.description: The number of partitions in a topic. You can increase the partition count for a topic, but you cannot decrease it. Increasing partitions for a topic that uses a key might change how messages are distributed.
partition_count.rationale: Affects performance and scalability, not security posture.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Used for scoping; no impact on access control or encryption.

replication_factor.description: The number of replicas of each partition. A replication factor of 3 is recommended for high availability.
replication_factor.rationale: Ensures data availability and fault tolerance. Lower replication factors increase the risk of data loss during failures.

topic_id.description: The ID to use for the topic, which will become the final component of the topic's name. This value is structured like: 'my-topic-name'.
topic_id.rationale: Used for naming the topic; does not affect access or data protection directly.
